title: Rational numbers as decimals
competency: Write rational numbers as terminating or repeating decimals, turn terminating decimals into fractions and locate rational numbers on the number line.

keywords.def: A decimal that ends, such as 0.6 or 2.375.
A decimal in which a block of digits repeats for ever, such as 0.333… or 0.2323…
A line over the repeating digits of a decimal: 0.3̅ means 0.333…
A line where every number has its own point. Numbers grow to the right.
A number that can be written a/b with integers a, b and b ≠ 0.

en.text: Divide a by b to write a/b as a decimal. Either the division stops, giving a terminating decimal like 0.6. Or the digits repeat for ever, like 0.555…. A bar over the repeating digits shows this. A terminating decimal becomes a fraction over 10, 100 or 1000.

am.text: a/bን በአስርዮሽ ለመጻፍ aን በb አካፍል። ወይ ማካፈሉ ይቆማል፤ እንደ 0.6 ያለ የሚያልቅ አስርዮሽ ይሰጣል። ወይ አሃዞቹ ለዘላለም ይደጋገማሉ፤ እንደ 0.555…። በሚደጋገሙት አሃዞች ላይ ያለ መስመር ይህንን ያሳያል። የሚያልቅ አስርዮሽ በ10፣ 100 ወይም 1000 ላይ ክፍልፋይ ይሆናል።

screens.title: Will the division stop?
screens.text: Divide 3 by 5 on paper. Then divide 5 by 9.
screens.ask: Which division do you think ends?
screens.after:
3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. The remainder becomes 0, so it ends.
5 ÷ 9 = 0.555… The remainder is 5 every time, so the 5s never stop.
Do both divisions, then read on.

screens.title: Two things can happen
paras: Any rational number a/b can be written as a decimal. Divide a by b.
The division may stop with remainder 0. Then it is a terminating decimal, such as 3/5 = 0.6.
Or the remainder never becomes 0 and the digits repeat. Then it is a repeating decimal, such as 5/9 = 0.555…
Bar notation. A bar over the repeating digits shows the repetition: 1/3 = 0.333… = 0.3̅ and 23/99 = 0.2323… = 0.2̅3̅.
screens.note: In long division, when a remainder comes back, the digits must repeat.

screens.title: Watch the remainders: 1 ÷ 7
steps: Remainder 1 is back. So the digits 142857 repeat: 1/7 = 0.1̅4̅2̅8̅5̅7̅.

screens.title: Name it
defs: A block of digits repeats for ever: 5/9 = 0.555…
A bar over the repeating block: 0.555… = 0.5̅.

screens.title: Which one ends?
screens.text: Terminating decimals: which fraction gives a terminating decimal?
screens.why:
Divide each one.
3 ÷ 8 = 0.375: the remainder reaches 0, so it ends.
1/3 = 0.333…, 2/9 = 0.222…, 5/6 = 0.8333…: they repeat.
So 3/8 gives a terminating decimal.
screens.clue: Divide each one. Which reaches remainder 0?

screens.title: Why 1/7 repeats
screens.text: Repeating decimals: why must the decimal for 1/7 repeat?
opts: The remainders can only be 1 to 6, so one must come back
screens.ans: The remainders can only be 1 to 6, so one must come back
screens.why:
When you divide by 7, each remainder is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6.
It never reaches 0 for 1/7, so only 1 to 6 are possible.
After at most 6 steps a remainder comes back.
Then the same digits follow again: 1/7 = 0.142857142857…
screens.clue: Divide 1 by 7 and watch the remainders.

screens.title: Terminating decimals to fractions
paras: A terminating decimal can be written as a fraction.
Use one zero for each digit after the decimal point.

screens.text: Count the digits after the point. Then simplify.
steps: GCF(18, 100) = 2. Divide top and bottom by 2.

screens.title: 0.45 as a fraction
screens.text: Decimal to fraction: write 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form.
screens.why:
0.45 has two decimal digits, so the denominator is 100.
0.45 = 45/100.
GCF(45, 100) = 5.
45 ÷ 5 = 9 and 100 ÷ 5 = 20. So 0.45 = 9/20.
(45/10 = 4.5, which is ten times too big.)
screens.clue: Two decimal digits means a denominator of 100.

screens.title: Bar notation
screens.text: Bar notation: which is 5/6 in bar notation?
screens.why:
Divide: 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333…
The 8 appears once. Only the 3 repeats.
So the bar goes over the 3 only: 0.83̅.
(0.8̅3̅ would mean 0.838383…, which is wrong.)

screens.title: Birr and santim
screens.text: Kebede pays 0.25 birr for a pencil eraser.
screens.ask: Decimal to fraction in simplest form: that is ___ birr.
screens.why:
0.25 has two decimal digits, so 0.25 = 25/100.
GCF(25, 100) = 25.
25 ÷ 25 = 1 and 100 ÷ 25 = 4.
So 0.25 birr = 1/4 birr (25 santim).
screens.clue: Two digits after the point: put 25 over 100, then simplify.
screens.worked: 0.25 has two decimal digits, so 0.25 = 25/100. GCF(25, 100) = 25. So 0.25 = 1/4.

screens.title: Divide it out
screens.ask: Fraction to decimal: 3/8 = ___ as a decimal.
screens.why:
Divide 3.000 by 8.
30 ÷ 8 = 3 r 6. 60 ÷ 8 = 7 r 4. 40 ÷ 8 = 5 r 0.
The remainder is 0, so the division stops.
So 3/8 = 0.375, a terminating decimal.

ideas.name: Rational numbers on the number line

en.text: Every rational number has a point on the number line. Integers are easy to mark. For a fraction, change it to a decimal first. For example, 4/3 = 1.333…, just past 1. And −5/2 = −2.5, halfway between −3 and −2.

am.text: እያንዳንዱ ምክንያታዊ ቁጥር በቁጥር መስመር ላይ ነጥብ አለው። ኢንቲጀሮችን ማመልከት ቀላል ነው። ክፍልፋይን መጀመሪያ ወደ አስርዮሽ ቀይር። ለምሳሌ 4/3 = 1.333… ከ1 ትንሽ ያልፋል። −5/2 = −2.5 ደግሞ በ−3 እና በ−2 መሃል ነው።

screens.title: Where does 4/3 sit?
screens.text: Picture a number line from −5 to 3.
screens.after:
4/3 = 1 + 1/3 = 1.333…
That is more than 1 and less than 2.
So 4/3 sits a third of the way from 1 to 2.

screens.title: Rational numbers on the number line
paras: Integers are easy. For fractions, change to decimals first.

screens.title: Figure 1.3: −5, 3, 4/3 and −5/2

points.info: is an integer: just count 5 left of 0.
= 1.333…, a third of the way from 1 to 2.

screens.ask: Tap each point to see where it sits.

screens.title: Name it
defs: A line where every number has a point. Every rational number has its place on it.

screens.title: Between which integers?
screens.text: Rational numbers on the number line: between which two integers is −5/2?
screens.why:
Change to a decimal: −5/2 = −2.5.
−2.5 is less than −2 and more than −3.
So −5/2 lies halfway between −3 and −2.
(−2 and −1 is a common slip: −2.5 is left of −2.)

screens.title: Which is further right?
screens.text: Comparing on the number line: which number is further to the right?
screens.why:
Write each as a decimal: 4/3 = 1.333…, 1.3, 1.2, −5/2 = −2.5.
Further right means larger.
1.333… > 1.3 > 1.2 > −2.5.
So 4/3 is furthest to the right.
screens.clue: Write each one as a decimal and compare.

screens.title: Temperature in Debre Birhan
screens.text: One cold morning in Debre Birhan the temperature was −3/2 °C.
screens.ask: Fraction to decimal: as a decimal, that is ___ °C.
screens.why:
Divide: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5.
Keep the minus sign: −3/2 = −1.5.
On the number line, −1.5 is halfway between −2 and −1.
So the temperature is −1.5 °C.
screens.clue: Divide 3 by 2, then keep the minus sign.
screens.worked: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5. Keep the sign: −3/2 = −1.5. On the line, it is halfway between −2 and −1.

screens.ask: Rational numbers on the number line: tap where −3/2 goes.
screens.why:
−3/2 = −1.5.
It is negative, so it is left of 0.
−1.5 is between −2 and −1, exactly halfway.
So −3/2 sits on the half mark between −2 and −1.

items.text: 1(a) Bar notation: write 8/9 with bar notation.
items.why:
Divide 8 by 9: 80 ÷ 9 = 8 r 8, and the remainder 8 comes back each time.
So 8/9 = 0.888…
One digit, 8, repeats.
So 8/9 = 0.8̅.

items.text: 1(c) Bar notation: write 1/11 with bar notation.
items.why:
Divide 1 by 11: 10 ÷ 11 = 0 r 10, 100 ÷ 11 = 9 r 1.
The remainder 1 comes back, so the digits repeat.
1/11 = 0.090909…
The block 09 repeats, so 1/11 = 0.0̅9̅.

items.text: 1(d) Bar notation: write 14/9 with bar notation.

items.why:
3/7 = 3 × 1/7, and 3/7 ≈ 0.43.
The sevenths use the same six digits 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 in a cycle.
Start the cycle at 4: 0.428571…
Check: 3 ÷ 7 = 0.428571428571…
So 3/7 = 0.4̅2̅8̅5̅7̅1̅.
items.clue: 3/7 is a bit less than 1/2. Which cycle starts near 0.43?

items.why:
0.77 has two digits after the point.
So the denominator is 100.
0.77 = 77/100.
GCF(77, 100) = 1, so it is already in simplest form.
items.clue: Count the digits after the point.

12.369 has three digits after the point.
So the denominator is 1000.

Keep the sign: −12.369 = −12369/1000.

items.text: Locate on the number line: where is 4/5?
items.why:
Change to a decimal: 4/5 = 0.8.
0.8 is between 0 and 1.
It is only 0.2 less than 1.
So 4/5 is just left of 1.

items.text: Locate on the number line: where is 2⅓?
opts: A third of the way from 2 to 3
A third of the way from 0 to 1
items.ans: A third of the way from 2 to 3
items.why:
2⅓ = 2 + 1/3 = 2.333…
It is between 2 and 3.
Split the gap from 2 to 3 into 3 equal parts.
2⅓ is at the first mark: a third of the way from 2 to 3.

test.text: Repeating decimals: which fraction gives a repeating decimal?
test.why:
Divide each one.
1/4 = 0.25, 3/5 = 0.6, 7/10 = 0.7: they end.
2/9 = 0.222…: the remainder 2 keeps coming back.
So 2/9 gives a repeating decimal.

test.ask: Decimal to fraction: −0.18 in simplest form is ___

test.text: Number line: 0.4̅ = 0.444… lies a little left of halfway between 0 and 1.
test.why:
Halfway between 0 and 1 is 0.5.
0.444… is less than 0.5.
So it lies a little left of halfway. True.

screens.title: Simplify 18/100
screens.text: Divide top and bottom by their GCF.
steps: Factors of 18 that also divide 100: 1 and 2.
So 18/100 = 9/50. GCF(9, 50) = 1, so it is in simplest form.

screens.title: Your turn
screens.text: Simplest form: what is 25/100 in simplest form?
screens.why:
Find GCF(25, 100): 100 = 4 × 25, so the GCF is 25.
25 ÷ 25 = 1 and 100 ÷ 25 = 4.
So 25/100 = 1/4.
(5/20 equals 1/4, but it is not yet in simplest form.)
screens.clue: Find the largest number that divides 25 and 100.
